close_reason: Added a 'Why an associated function and not a method' rustdoc section on JmapBackend::principal_id that explains the deliberate omission of &self. The signature structurally enforces the 'identity is not the JMAP layer's job to mint' rule: auth-layer middleware MUST pre-resolve the principal and stash the result in CallerCtx before calling dispatch(). JIT lookup is not possible from inside principal_id. Documented so a future contributor doesn't file the 'why isn't this a method' PR.
description:
Scenario: a future *-server consumer (or a third-party building on jmap-server) implements JmapBackend with CallerCtx = JwtClaims { sub: String, ... } — the upstream auth layer hands the handler a parsed JWT but not yet a resolved local principal Id. The backend wants to map sub → Id via an internal lookup table or database call. Today: JmapBackend::principal_id (crate-jmap-server/src/backend.rs:777) is declared as fn principal_id(caller: &Self::CallerCtx) — no &self. The backend has no way to access its own state from inside principal_id, so the JWT→Id mapping cannot live there.

The docstring is explicit: 'Implementations MUST NOT mint identity — they MUST read it from the CallerCtx populated by the HTTP/auth middleware before dispatch() was called.' The structural absence of &self enforces the rule. That is a real engineering decision, not an accident.

The cost: every consumer that wants per-request principal resolution must do it in the HTTP layer (before dispatch) and stash the result in CallerCtx. This is workable but rigid — it pushes auth integration up a layer and forbids JIT lookup. The reference impl (jmapchat-server) and the kith/stoa consumers already match this pattern, so it's fine for the *known* consumers; but the docs nowhere admit the tradeoff.

Recommendation: keep the signature as is, but add a paragraph to the doc comment naming the structural choice: 'principal_id is an associated function, not a method, by design — backends cannot use &self to resolve identity at JMAP-call time. The auth-layer middleware MUST pre-resolve the principal and populate CallerCtx before dispatch().' Three sentences saves a future contributor from filing a 'why isn't this a method' PR you'd reject.

Maintenance consequence: low frequency, real PR overhead when someone hits it. Documenting the rationale up front is the cheap fix.
title: principal_id is an associated function not a method, locking out backends that need &self to resolve identity
